key_insight: PoreML unifies pore-scale data generation, training, and evaluation to make multiphase flow prediction in porous media more reliable and reproducible.
engineering_relevance: The framework can accelerate design and optimization for CO2 storage, fuel cells, and packaging by providing a shared benchmark for learning complex interface dynamics in realistic porous geometries.
method: GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver for reproducible pore-scale simulation data
3.3 TB dataset with 560 runs and 158,546 time steps across synthetic and micro-CT-based structures
Unified evaluation for one-step prediction, autoregressive rollouts, and physics consistency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports five evaluated models, two transfer challenges, and a large multi-scenario dataset spanning diverse wettability and viscosity ratios.
watch_item: Generalization may remain difficult when moving to larger domains or from synthetic to micro-CT-derived structures, so transfer performance should be checked carefully.
paper_title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
